subject.title: Rebrand text-substitution filter on tool-call arguments silently misroutes file ops

question: What permanent boundary should plugin text transforms have for path-bearing prompts and executable tool-call arguments?
rationale: Current behavior is documented and intentionally restores structured tool-call args, but the issue shows that the same broad string rewrite can misroute filesystem operations; automation cannot choose that compatibility boundary safely.

options.title: Path-safe transform boundary
options.body: Keep text transforms for normal prompt/output compatibility, but skip or validate replacements in filesystem/tool-input contexts and add tests/docs for that boundary.

options.title: No tool-argument transforms
options.body: Disable output transforms for executable tool-call arguments entirely, accepting that masking/normalization plugins must use before_tool_call for argument rewrites.

options.title: Keep broad transforms
options.body: Preserve current broad semantics and document before_tool_call or deployment-specific configuration as the escape hatch, leaving this report as unsupported behavior.

recommendation.title: Path-safe transform boundary
recommendation.body: Keep text transforms for normal prompt/output compatibility, but skip or validate replacements in filesystem/tool-input contexts and add tests/docs for that boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature-history evidence points to steipete as the introducer of the text-transform surface and the best available owner for the compatibility boundary decision.
